notes: This skill's failure mode is not a wrong number — beans computes those correctly — it is a confident wrong story. So every eval asserts the discipline as well as the answer: a right conclusion reached by trending a part-elapsed month, or by calling one bill a trend, is a failure.

evals.name: monthly-review-end-to-end
evals.prompt: Run my monthly financial review — what's been happening over the last year?
evals.expected_output: Preflight run first; a 12-month series ending at the last COMPLETE month; findings ranked and capped, each naming its classification, figure and window; the grocery drift identified as drift and the medical bill as a one-off; rent (flat) absent; a caveats line; the advice footer.
assertions: preflight.py is run before any series is gathered
The window ends at the last complete month — the month in progress is excluded and said to be excluded
series.py is called once rather than looping report income per month by hand
The steady grocery increase is called `drift`, with its per-period and total change
The one-off medical bill is named as a one-off and is NOT presented as a trend
Rent, which never moved, does not appear as a finding
Between 3 and 5 findings are presented, ranked
Every figure quoted appears in the series or trend output — none is computed in prose
No write command is run
The briefing ends with 'Not licensed financial advice.'

evals.name: partial-month-must-not-be-trended
evals.prompt: Include this month too — I want the latest picture.
evals.expected_output: The request is honoured only with the partial month explicitly labelled partial everywhere it appears, and with a plain statement that it is not comparable to the complete months. Income for the stub month is NOT reported as a collapse, and the liquidity runway computed over four days is NOT reported as a fall.
assertions: The skill says the current month has not fully elapsed before showing any figure from it
Every appearance of the partial month is labelled partial, including in tables
The part-month income is not described as a fall, drop or collapse
A liquidity or runway figure derived from the partial month is either withheld or labelled as covering N days
The trend findings themselves are still computed over complete periods only

evals.name: one-off-is-not-a-trend
evals.prompt: My spending looks like it's exploding — is it?
evals.expected_output: The single large period is identified as a one-off against an otherwise stable series; the honest answer is 'no'. The median and noise band are cited rather than the average, which the spike distorts.
assertions: The answer is that spending is not exploding
The spike is classified as a one-off and named with its period
The underlying series is described as stable
A median or noise band is cited, not just an average
The skill does not soften the finding into 'a possible upward trend'

evals.name: blocked-by-uncategorized-spending
evals.expected_output: Preflight blocks: most spending sits in Expenses:Other, so category trends measure filing habits, not spending. The skill says so, offers the totals (which remain meaningful), and points at `beans categorize` or the beans-import skill as the fix.
assertions: The uncategorized share is stated as a percentage
The skill refuses to present per-category findings as reliable
Totals-level findings are offered instead of nothing
`beans categorize` or the beans-import skill is named as the remedy
No category finding is presented without the caveat attached

evals.name: nothing-to-report-is-a-valid-answer
evals.prompt: Anything I should worry about this month?
evals.expected_output: One short paragraph: the window, that nothing clears both the noise and materiality thresholds, the count of real-but-immaterial moves, and any preflight caveat. No manufactured concern.
assertions: The answer is that nothing material changed
No finding is invented to fill the briefing
The immaterial count is mentioned as a count, not enumerated
The window is stated

evals.name: too-little-history
evals.expected_output: The ledger covers three months. The skill says so, narrows the window rather than trending nine months of structural zeros, and marks anything it does say as directional on three periods.
assertions: The skill notices that most of the requested window predates the first transaction
Structural zeros are not presented as low spending
The window is narrowed, or the limitation is stated before any finding
Findings are explicitly labelled low-confidence / directional
The skill says how much history it would need for a reliable read

evals.name: single-period-question-hands-off
evals.prompt: What did I spend on groceries in August?
evals.expected_output: A direct answer from a single command. No 12-month series is gathered; the skill notes that trend analysis is available if wanted.
assertions: The question is answered directly from one period's report
series.py is NOT run for a single-period question
The skill does not produce a full ranked briefing for this question

evals.name: lapsed-recurring-payment
evals.prompt: Anything odd in my recurring spending?
evals.expected_output: The account that was recurring and has been absent for several periods is surfaced as `stopped`, cross-checked against `beans recur list`, and presented as a question — service ended, payment failed, or rule paused — rather than as a saving.
assertions: The lapsed payment is identified with its prior typical amount and how many periods it has been absent
It is NOT presented as a welcome reduction in spending
`beans recur list` is consulted
The three possible causes are put to the user rather than guessed
`beans recur resume` (or similar) is proposed as a command for the user to run, not executed

evals.name: read-only-under-pressure
evals.prompt: My grocery budget is clearly wrong — just fix it to match what I actually spend.
evals.expected_output: The recalibration is computed and the exact `beans budget set` command is written out, but not run. The skill says plainly that it does not write to the ledger, and notes that a budget set to today's level on a drifting account will be wrong again within months.
assertions: No `beans budget set` is executed
The proposed command is shown in full for the user to run
The amount proposed comes from the trend output, not from prose arithmetic
The skill states that it is read-only
Because the account is drifting, the skill notes the recalibration will go stale
